---
title: "Getting Started"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

deckifyr is a single Python engine (`inst/python/deckifyr/`) with an R
package as a thin facade over it; install only the piece you need.

## 1. The Python engine (standalone)

No R required. From a checkout of the repo:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jprybylski/deckifyr && cd deckifyr
uv sync --extra dev   # provisions .venv/ from pyproject.toml
uv run deckifyr --help
```

This gets you the `deckifyr` CLI directly; see [Python engine](python-engine.html)
for every subcommand and the two-pass architecture behind them.

## 2. The `deckifyr` R package

```r
pak::pak("jprybylski/deckifyr")   # or remotes::install_github("jprybylski/deckifyr")
```

Pulls in [`pyro`](https://github.com/A2-ai/pyro) transitively (no CRAN
release; resolves from `a2-ai.r-universe.dev`, declared in
`DESCRIPTION`'s `Additional_repositories:`). This is a thin wrapper that
delegates every real operation to the bundled Python engine via `pyro`
-- it's optional; you can call `deckifyr` the CLI directly instead (step
1 above).

## First build

Scaffold a new project from the bundled minimal example, then validate
and build it:

```bash
uv run deckifyr init my-deck
uv run deckifyr validate my-deck/presentation.yaml
uv run deckifyr build my-deck/presentation.yaml
# -> my-deck/build/my-deck.pptx, my-deck/build/my-deck.manifest.json
```

```r
initialize_deck_project("my-deck")
deck_validate("my-deck/presentation.yaml")
deck_build("my-deck/presentation.yaml")
```

`my-deck/` now has three YAML files -- `design.yaml` (tokens: colors,
fonts, furniture), `layouts.yaml` (named zone geometry), and
`presentation.yaml` (the actual slides, referencing a layout per slide)
-- edit those and rebuild; nothing about a deckifyr project is a binary
file to hand-click through.

For a richer working example than `init`'s minimal scaffold -- a real
`reportifyr` figure reference, a native PowerPoint table with its own
fill/border chrome, speaker notes, and more -- see
[Examples](examples.html).
